newsitem.title: FRANCE: Donor nations pledge support for Malawi.
newsitem.headline: Donor nations pledge support for Malawi.

text.p: Donor nations pledged $319 million to Malawi in 1997 and urged the southern African nation to pursue poverty relief and economic reform to boost private investment, the World Bank said on Wednesday.
The donors pledged a further $346 million for 1998 and $234 million for 1999 which will cover all but $139 million of the country's financing needs for the two years, the Bank said.
About one third of the 1997 pledge amount was in the form of grants with the remaining two thirds in loans.
Donors, who applauded reform efforts so far, also urged Malawi to start an "active dialogue" to reduce its debt burden.
"Confirmed pledges plus indicative announcements made at the meeting are expected to meet fully Malawi's external financing needs in 1997," the World Bank said in a statement.
Donor nations praised Malawi's success in cutting its budget deficit by 20 percentage points and lowering inflation to about seven percent from 75 percent over the last two years.

Malawi is one of the poorest countries in the world and suffers from a very high rate of HIV infection, particularly among its women, said Terence Jones, resident representative in Malawi for the the United Nations Development Program.
Jones said the government hopes the Malawi economy will grow by between six and seven percent a year.
He said the support from donors was due to the government's commitment to liberalising the economy, reforming the political process and redistributing vast estate land holdings.
He said there was a consensus among the donors that Malawi had to pay more attention to the bottom layer of the country's poor and to women, long oppressed in Malawi culture.
